Taper

TAY-per -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, TAY; sounds like 'tape' plus '-er.' · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To taper to gradually lessen or reduce something.

The kayak's bow tapers to a point that slices cleanly through the water.

Worked Example

The carpenter clamps a square table leg to her bench and runs the plane along it, stroke after stroke, taking a little more wood near the floor end each pass. When she stands it up, the leg flows from full thickness at the top to a slim, elegant foot.

She tapered the leg: reduced it gradually toward an end point. That end point is taper's signature. A candle tapers to its tip, a storm tapers off to nothing, a training plan tapers down to race day -- always a smooth slope aimed at a finish, never a sudden cut.

How Taper Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

narrow

narrow: to become thinner toward one end

dwindle

dwindle: to shrink steadily away

decrease

decrease: to become less

Antonyms

widen

widen: to grow broader

expand

expand: to increase in size or extent

How Strong Is It? — decrease → taper → dwindle

decrease vs. taper

decrease vs. taper: Decrease just says the amount drops, in any pattern, while taper insists on the shape of the drop: smooth, gradual, and headed for an end point.

dwindle vs. taper

dwindle vs. taper: Dwindle is the strongest fade-out: supplies that dwindle are slipping toward nothing whether anyone plans it or not, while a taper is usually deliberate -- a dose, a schedule, or a shape eased down on purpose.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — tapor

root — tapor: a slender candle (Old English tapor, of uncertain origin)

Put it together

Put it together: A taper was first a thing, not an action: Old English tapor, a slim candle thick at the base and narrowing to the wick. The candle's shape became the verb -- to taper is to do what the candle does, thinning gradually toward a tip. The word's deeper origin is unsettled, which is why it is marked uncertain.

Use the root in a new word: tapered

Use the root in a new word: tapered: Jeans with tapered legs narrow gradually from the knee to the ankle.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Taper works two ways, both aimed at an end point: physically, a thing tapers when it narrows toward a tip (a candle, a kayak bow, a trail); over time, something tapers OFF when it winds down gradually (a storm, a medication dose, a training schedule). Keep it apart from its unit-mates: atrophy blames disuse, wither means drying up, and ebb recedes like a tide that may return -- a taper is a one-way slope to a finish.
